home.title: Kinetic Code
home.subtitle: Mechatronics, code, and the stubbornness of someone who wants to understand how things really work.
home.bodyHtml:
This is the technical journal of a mechatronics engineer who spends the day between PLCs, C++, and cables that should not smoke — but sometimes do anyway. No ready-made tutorials, no LinkedIn fluff: here you find the real process. Bugs solved the hard way, machine cycles optimized bit by bit, design decisions made — and sometimes wrong — in front of an electrical cabinet at two in the morning.

If you are curious about the exact point where software meets metal, you are in the right place.

about.title: Who writes this, without too many words
about.bodyHtml:
I am a mechatronics engineer. I work at the point where software meets real machines: PLCs that speak Modbus, motors that must turn in the right direction, firmware that cannot afford to crash while a 200-ton press is closing its mold.

You will not find my name, my age, or where I come from here — that is not the point. The point is the work: years spent on the production floor doing testing and commissioning, debugging C++ and Qt systems, hours spent understanding why a machine cycle slows down by forty milliseconds that no customer will ever notice, but that keep me up at night.

Kinetic Code was born from a simple observation: in the age of mass-produced content, the real value is in showing the actual work — the failed attempts, the architectures rethought three times, the before-and-after charts of an optimization. Not copy-paste tutorials, but reasoning, explained the way it would happen in front of a whiteboard.

I use artificial intelligence tools the way you would use a very fast junior colleague: it proposes, I verify, I sign off. The code you see here, the architectural choices, the tests on real hardware — they are mine, verified in the field before becoming an article.

If you work in automation, in embedded systems, or you simply enjoy understanding how things are built from the inside: welcome.
about.contactText: Questions about something you read, curiosity about a specific setup, or a professional inquiry — design review, architecture advice, consulting work: write to kineticcode.dev@gmail.com. I read and answer everything myself.
